Class CharacterList

java.lang.Object
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.StoryGraphCollection<Character>
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.StoryGraphList<Character>
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.SymbolList<Character>
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.CharacterList
All Implemented Interfaces:
Iterable<Character>, RandomAccess
public class CharacterList extends SymbolList<Character>
The list of characters, or agents, who take actions and have possibly wrong beliefs in a story graph. Characters can be player characters or non-player characters.
Author:
Stephen G. Ware

    • add

      public Character add(String name)
      Description copied from class: SymbolList
      Creates a new symbol of this type with the given name, or returns the existing symbol with that name if one already exists. If a new symbol is created, its ID number will be the next in the sequence (i.e. the size of this collection at the time the symbol is created).

      This method updates the story graph's meta-data with the new number of symbols of this type. It also updates the last modified timestamp.

      Specified by:
      add in class SymbolList<Character>
      Parameters:
      name - the name of the symbol to create or find
      Returns:
      a new symbol with that given name, or the existing symbol with that name if one already exists

    • setPlayer

      public void setPlayer(Character character, boolean value)
      Marks as character is a player character or a non-player character. Player characters are typically controlled by the person experiencing an interactive narrative, whereas non-player characters are typically controlled by the story author.

      If this method modified the character, it updates the story graph's meta-data last modified timestamp.

      Parameters:
      character - any character
      value - true to set the character as a player character, or false to set the character as a non-player character

    • sort

      public boolean sort(Comparator<? super Character> comparator, Status status)
      Sorts and renumbers the symbols of this collection based on the given comparator. If the order of any symbols changes, their ID numbers will be reassigned to be sequential.

      If this method modifies the order of elements, it updates the story graph's meta-data last modified timestamp.

      If this method reorders any of the characters in this collection, it will also modify all of the utility values in the graph's state objects to reflect the new order of characters, which can take a long time if there are many state objects.

      Overrides:
      sort in class SymbolList<Character>
      Parameters:
      comparator - the comparator that defines the new order of elements
      status - a status object that will be updated while this method runs to reflect its current progress
      Returns:
      true if any elements were reordered, false if all elements remained in the same order

    • remove

      public boolean remove(Predicate<? super Character> predicate, Status status)
      Description copied from class: StoryGraphList
      Removes all elements from this collection for which the given predicate returns true. This method may modify other elements of the story graph and may run for a long time as a result. For example, when nodes are removed from a story graph, all edges incident to those nodes are also removed.

      If the graph was modified by this method, the elements in this collection and other elements of the graph will be renumbered.

      This method will also update the story graph's meta-data with the new number of elements of this type and the last modified timestamp.

      Overrides:
      remove in class StoryGraphList<Character>
      Parameters:
      predicate - a predicate that specifies which elements should be removed
      status - a status object that will be updated while this method runs to reflect its current progress
      Returns:
      true if any elements were removed and the graph was modified, false if nothing was removed and the graph was not modified
